title: Thermoelectric figure of merit above 3
bottleneck: Thermoelectric efficiency is governed by zT, and despite decades of nanostructuring, values remain stuck near 1-2 for practical materials because raising electrical conductivity also raises thermal conductivity — the fundamental trade-off. Lab reports of higher zT often rely on measurement artifacts or unstable compositions that do not survive device integration. No material has demonstrated zT above 3 in a stable, manufacturable device.
why_it_blocks: Waste heat is one of the largest untapped energy sources: industry and vehicles reject most input energy as heat. Without high-zT materials, thermoelectric recovery stays confined to niche applications like deep-space probes instead of cutting global fuel use.
current_state: Skutterudites and half-Heusler alloys have reached module-level zT near 1.5 with improving stability, and automotive waste-heat prototypes exist. But the economics only work at much higher efficiency, which no known material system credibly promises.
